summary: Wesson Coulomb logarithm estimate for the declared collision pair.

capability: Wesson Coulomb logarithm ln Lambda for electron-ion collisions from temperature in keV and density in m^-3.
operation: Evaluate the Wesson electron-ion Coulomb logarithm
discovery.model: Wesson Coulomb-log relation ln Lambda = 31.3 - 0.5 ln(n_e) + ln(1000 T_e) with explicit numeric boundary checks.
discovery.geometry: Homogeneous plasma point with broadcast T_e and n_e arrays; no spatial geometry is inferred.
discovery.boundary: T_e in keV and n_e in m^-3 must be finite and strictly positive.

identity.definition: 31.3-0.5*ln(n_e)+ln(1000*T_e); keV is converted to eV by the factor 1000. Evaluation uses ln(1000)+ln(T), avoiding intermediate overflow/underflow.
identity.model: Wesson Coulomb-log relation with explicit SciRel numeric boundary checks
identity.boundary: strictly positive finite T_e in keV and n_e in m^-3
assumptions: This is a mathematical weak-coupling estimate.
The caller decides whether a positive/adequate Coulomb logarithm is physically applicable.

inputs.name: T_e
inputs.dtype: real integer/float numeric scalar or array-like; converted to float64
inputs.constraints: finite and strictly positive; nonempty, boolean/string/complex/masked values rejected

inputs.name: n_e
inputs.dtype: real integer/float numeric scalar or array-like; converted to float64
inputs.constraints: finite and strictly positive; nonempty, boolean/string/complex/masked values rejected

outputs.name: result
outputs.constraints: Finite signed mathematical formula value; physical suitability for a collision model is caller-owned.

preconditions: strictly positive finite T_e in keV and n_e in m^-3

Above the formulary's 10 Z^2 eV condition (10 eV at Z = 1) the caller accepts the high-temperature (quantum cutoff) branch; below it the relation warns and still returns the value. The table conditions both e-i branches on more than T_e: T_i*m_e/m_i < T_e < 10 Z^2 eV selects the low-temperature form, T_i*m_e/m_i < 10 Z^2 eV < T_e the high-temperature one, and a T_e < T_i*m_e/m_i branch is listed as well. This interface accepts neither T_i nor an ion mass and fixes Z = 1 for electrons, so those conditions stay the caller's judgement.
supported: Finite NumPy evaluation of the declared relation and broadcast shape on the quantum-cutoff branch, valid above the declared T_e ~ 10 Z^2 eV boundary (10 eV here; that boundary is transcribed from the NRL Plasma Formulary 2016 printed p. 34 table and was maintainer-checked in #212, while the Wesson edition and section remain UNKNOWN).
excluded: Whole-transport evolution, experimental calibration, and implicit coordinate reconstruction.
Interpreting zero or negative computed logarithms as valid weakly coupled collision physics; physical calibration or a regime-switching model.

The low-temperature electron-ion classical-cutoff branch (a classical-cutoff form 23 - ln(n_e^0.5 Z T_e^-1.5), T_e in eV, n_e in cm^-3; transcribed from the NRL Plasma Formulary 2016 printed p. 34 table, maintainer-checked in #212) is not provided: below 10 eV the returned quantum-branch value only warns, and it sits above that form by about +37% at n_e = 1e17 m^-3, +55.5% at 1e19 and +112% at 1e21 (0.1 eV; the gap grows with density). The two forms cross near 16.2 eV, above which the quantum form reads lower.
The low-temperature e-i estimate is not provided as a public relation: below 10 Z^2 eV the returned high-temperature estimate differs from it and only warns.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for boolean/string/complex/masked or empty input, non-finite values, malformed or incompatible shape, and the nonpositive or singular domains named by the callable contract.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises FloatingPointError if accepted finite inputs produce an unrepresentable output; no fallback is returned. Emits scirel.ApplicabilityWarning when any input temperature is below 10 Z^2 eV (10 eV at Z = 1), the part of the source's e-i branch conditions this interface can evaluate; the table also conditions both branches on T_i*m_e/m_i, which this signature cannot evaluate (no T_i or ion mass, Z = 1), so the remaining conditions stay the caller's judgement. The message names the lowest input, the low-temperature branch, and the gap to the NRL Plasma Formulary e-i branches, 2016 printed p.34 (PPPL official copy), as transcribed from the original table (see #197, #212): 24 - ln(sqrt(n_e)/T_e) for T_e > 10 Z^2 eV and 23 - ln(sqrt(n_e) Z T_e^(-3/2)) below it, T_e in eV and n_e in cm^-3; the returned relation keeps constant 31.3, about 0.392 above that branch's converted constant 24 + ln 1000 = 30.907755... The value is returned unchanged.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this is a direct algebraic mapping.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No output is returned after an exception.

example.description: Run the relation on a finite declared-domain case.
example.code:
import warnings
import numpy as np
from scirel.physics import calculate_log_lambda_ei
r=calculate_log_lambda_ei(2., 1e19)
assert np.isfinite(r)
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    low = calculate_log_lambda_ei(0.005, 1e19)
assert np.isfinite(low) and len(caught) == 1
example.expected: A finite Coulomb logarithm for the in-range sample, plus one ApplicabilityWarning for the below-10-eV sample whose value is returned unchanged.

scope: Independent 60-digit Decimal logarithms over temperature/density/charge scales including smallest subnormal and largest float64; transformation/scaling identities.
Declared failure cases for empty, boolean/string/complex/masked, nonfinite and incompatible inputs.
Agreement with the canonical SciRel callers and dependencies of this relation.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Maintained tests establish the named relation, shape and selected boundary behavior only; they do not establish global physical calibration.
known_limitations: No external calibration or collision-frequency composition is claimed.
Only the Wesson algebra and declared numerical boundaries are covered.

The existing relation 31.3 - ln(sqrt(n_e)/T_e[eV]) was historically attributed to Sauter et al. (1999) as lnLambda_e in the electron collisionality nu*_e. That attribution and its original equation have not been verified and remain UNKNOWN, on the same footing as Wesson below. The 'ee' function (constant 31.0) is a different estimate.

The e-i branches and their T_e > 10 Z^2 eV condition come from the NRL Plasma Formulary, 2016 printed p.34, transcribed from the original table and checked by the maintainer (see #197, #212). The table additionally conditions both branches on T_i*m_e/m_i and lists a T_e < T_i*m_e/m_i branch, and this interface cannot evaluate those (no T_i or ion mass, Z = 1). The ~16.2 eV intersection with the low-temperature branch is algebra on a formula extrapolated outside its own range; it is not a physical switching point and not an accuracy criterion.

The gap to the low-temperature branch is an algebraic difference between two estimates, not an error against measured physics: at n_e = 1e19 m^-3 it is +55.54% at 0.1 eV and +17.33% at 1 eV, and it grows with density, so the warning computes it per sample.

The Wesson attribution of constant 31.3, edition and section were not verified and remain UNKNOWN; the NRL transcription recorded above is a separate, maintainer-checked fact (see #197, #212), so the two provenance states are kept apart rather than combined.

The existing implementation keeps constant 31.3. The NRL high-temperature e-i expression, with density converted to m^-3 and temperature left in eV, has constant 24 + ln 1000 = 30.907755...; for this interface's keV input its temperature term is ln(1000*T_e). The constants differ by about 0.392 in the logarithm. This is a numerical comparison of the existing implementation and the maintainer-checked NRL transcription, not verification of a second published source. The original-source attribution of 31.3 and the origin of the difference remain UNKNOWN.
